questions.question: Which among the following rulers adopted the title devaputra?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kushana.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kushana** adopted the title **devaputra,** which means** "son of god".**
 
• Kushanas were a **Central Asian dynasty** that ruled over parts of South Asia during the **1st to 3rd centuries CE.**
 
• The title **devaputra **was used to signify the **divine status of the ruler** and their connection to the gods.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hoyasala **was a **South Indian dynasty** that ruled over parts of **Karnataka** during the 10th to 14th centuries CE.
 
• **Chola **was a South Indian dynasty that ruled over parts of **Tamil Nadu **during the 9th to 13th centuries CE. 
 
• **Saka** were a **Central Asian dynasty** that ruled over parts of **South Asia **during the 2nd century BCE to 4th century CE.

questions.question: What was the theme of International Yoga Day (2022)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Yoga for Humanity.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The theme of International Yoga Day (2022) was** "Yoga for Humanity".**
 
• Yoga for Humanity is a theme that emphasizes the role of yoga in creating a better world by promoting** peace, harmony, and universal brotherhood**.
 
• It aims to bring people from different **cultures, religions, and backgrounds together** and unite them in a common pursuit of **well-being and happiness.**
 
• The theme highlights the importance of yoga in promoting **physical, mental, and spiritual health**.
 
• It also recognizes the role of yoga in reducing** stress, anxiety, and depression**, and improving overall quality of life.
 
• The theme encourages people to **practice yoga **not only for their own benefit but also for the benefit of others.
 
• It emphasizes the need for **selfless service, compassion, and empathy** towards all living beings.
 
• The theme also promotes the idea of** sustainable livin**g and encourages people to adopt an **eco-friendly lifestyle.**
 
• It recognizes the need to** protect the environment** and preserve the **natural resources** for future generations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
• **"Yoga for Good Body"** emphasizes the role of yoga in improving** physical health and fitness**.

 
 
• It recognizes the benefits of yoga in **building strength, flexibility, and endurance.**
 
• While this is an important aspect of yoga, it **does not** capture the holistic nature of the practice.
 
 
 
• **"Yoga for Good Mind" **focuses on the** mental and emotional benefits **of yoga.
 
 
• It recognizes the role of yoga in reducing **stress, anxiety, and depression, **and improving mental clarity and focus.
 
• While this is an important aspect of yoga, it **does no**t capture the broader social and environmental dimensions of the practice.
 
 
 
• **"Yoga for Life" **is a general theme that highlights the importance of yoga in promoting **overall well-being and longevity**.
 
 
• While this theme is broad and inclusive, it **does not **provide a specific focus or direction for the practice.

questions.question: In which of the following articles, “Right of minorities to establish and administer educational institution” is mentioned?

• **Article 30 **of the Indian Constitution mentions the **right of minorities **to establish and administer **educational institutions.**
 
• This article gives the right to minorities, whether based on** religion or language,** to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice.
 
• The purpose of this article is to protect the** cultural and educational rights of minorities** and ensure that they are not deprived of the opportunity to conserve their **language, script, or culture.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Article 31** relates to the **right to property.**
 
• **Article 28 **deals with the **freedom of religious instruction.**
 
• **Article 30A** provides for the reservation of **seats in educational institutions** for socially and educationally backward classes of citizens.

questions.question: The broad, green part of the leaf is called _______.

__
 
• The** broad green part **of the leaf is known as **lamina,** which is also referred to as the** leaf blade.**
 
• The lamina is the main part of the leaf that is responsible for **photosynthesis**, as it contains the **chlorophyll pigment.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The **midrib** is the central vein that runs down the **center of the leaf blade,** providing support and structure to the leaf.

questions.question: According to _______ law, heat produced by an electric current is directly proportional to the resistance of the conductor, the square of the current, and the time for which it flows.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Joule's.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Joule's law** states that the amount of heat produced in a conductor is directly proportional to the** resistance **of the conductor, the **square of the current**, and the** time **for which it flows. 
 
• This law is also known as the **law of heating or the Joule-Lenz law.**
 
• The law is important in the study of **electrical circuits,** as it helps to determine the amount of **heat generated** in the circuit, which can affect the performance and safety of the circuit.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hooke's law** states that the force required to extend or compress a spring is directly proportional to the **distance of extension or compression.**
 
• **Charles's law **states that the **volume of a gas** is directly proportional to its **absolute temperature **at constant pressure.
 
• **Faraday's law **states that the **electromotive force (EMF)** induced in a closed circuit is directly proportional to the rate of change of** magnetic flux** through the circuit.

questions.question: Seasonal reversal in the wind direction during a year refers to ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Monsoon.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Seasonal reversal** in the wind direction during a year is a phenomenon that occurs due to the** differential heating of land **and **water bodies.**
 
• This results in the **formation of low-pressure areas** over land during summers and **high-pressure areas** over oceans during winters, which causes the **reversal of wind direction.**
 
• **Monsoon** is a **weather phenomenon** that is characterized by seasonal changes in the **wind direction**, which brings heavy rainfall in some regions.
 
• It is commonly associated with the Indian subcontinent, but it also occurs in other parts of the world such as **Southeast Asia, West Africa, and Australia.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Emission** refers to the release of **gases, particles, or other substances** into the atmosphere, which can have adverse effects on the environment and human health.

 
 
• It is often caused by human activities such as** burning fossil fuels **and **industrial processes.**
 
 
 
• **Breeze** is a gentle wind that is often associated with **pleasant weather conditions.**
 
 
• It can be caused by the** differential heating of land and water bodies**, as well as other natural factors such as the rotation of the earth and the movement of **high-pressure and low-pressure systems. **
 
 
 
• **Climate** refers to the long-term patterns of **temperature, humidity, precipitation**, and other weather variables in a given region.
 
 
• It is affected by a variety of factors such as **solar radiation, ocean currents, atmospheric circulation, and human activities.**

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT part of six school of Indian Philosophy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dravida.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dravida** is not a school of Indian philosophy.
 
• Dravida is a term used to refer to the** southern part of India.**
 
• **Samkhya** is one of the **oldest schools of Indian philosophy** that focuses on the** dualism of matter and spirit.**
 
• It believes in the existence of **Purusha (consciousness) and Prakriti (matter)** and their interplay.
 
• **Yoga** is a school of Indian philosophy that emphasizes the practice of **physical, mental, and spiritual disciplines** to attain liberation or Moksha.
 
• It is based on the** Yoga Sutras of Patanjali.**
 
• **Nyaya **is a school of Indian philosophy that focuses on** logic and reasoning.**
 
• It aims to establish the validity of** knowledge and perception **through inference and deduction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian philosophy** is a vast field that encompasses various schools of thought, each with its unique approach and philosophy.
 
• The six schools of Indian philosophy are **Samkhya, Yoga, Nyaya, Vaisheshika, Mimamsa, and Vedanta. **
 
• **Vaisheshika** is a school of Indian philosophy that focuses on **metaphysics and epistemology.**
 
• It believes in the** existence of atoms** and their combination to form matter.
 
• **Mimamsa** is a school of Indian philosophy that focuses on the interpretation of** Vedic texts and rituals.**
 
• It aims to establish the correct meaning and purpose of the** Vedic texts.**
 
• **Vedanta** is a school of Indian philosophy that focuses on the **Upanishads **and the concept of the **ultimate reality or Brahman.**
 
• It emphasizes the unity of the individual self or **Atman with Brahman.**

• The Bill also provides for the **confidentiality of the mediation process **and prohibits the use of information obtained during mediation in any other legal proceedings.

questions.question: Annapurna Devi was known to practice which musical instrument?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Surbahar.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Annapurna Devi **was a renowned Indian classical musician who belonged to the **Maihar Gharana.**
 
• She was born in **1927 in Maihar, Madhya Pradesh**, India.
 
• She was known to practice the **Surbahar,** which is a **stringed instrument** similar to the sitar but with a** lower tone.**
 
• Annapurna Devi was considered a **master of this instrument** and was one of the few female musicians to achieve such recognition in her time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Sarod** is another stringed instrument that is popular in **Indian classical music.**

 
 
• It has a **deeper sound** than the sitar and is played with a **pick**.
 
• The Sarod is often used in **North Indian classical music. **
 
 
 
• **The Violin **is a Western classical instrument that is played with a **bow.**
 
 
• It is **not** commonly used in Indian classical music, although some musicians have experimented with incorporating it into their performances.
 
 
 
• The** Bamboo Flute **is a wind instrument that is commonly used in** Indian classical music.**
 
 
• It is also known as the **Bansuri** and is made from** bamboo reeds of varying sizes**.
 
• It is often used to **create melodic lines **in performances.

questions.question: "India at Risk" is written by which of the following authors?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jaswant Singh.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"India at Risk"** is written by **Jaswant Singh.**
 
• Jaswant Singh was a politician and author who served as the **Minister of External Affairs and Finance Minister** of India.
 
• The book "India at Risk" discusses various issues that pose a** risk to India's security and stability**, such as terrorism, corruption, and economic challenges.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Khushwant Singh **was also an author, but he is known for his works of **fiction and non-fiction **that explore the cultural and social dynamics of India.
 
• **Natwar Singh** was a diplomat and politician who served as the **Minister of External Affairs of India.**
 
• **Vijay Darda **is a politician and businessman.
